goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:19 — Imported feed/HTML is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered via `raw post.cooked`, so any RSS item or scraped page containing <script>/onerror yields stored XSS on the forum.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html`, and `Post#cook` now returns `raw` directly when `cook_method == raw_html`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `skip_validations: true` and `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using `contents` sourced from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed`: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) or scraped HTML (`import_remote`), and `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative URLs without stripping dangerous tags/attributes. The embed view then renders posts with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any embedded `<script>` tag or event-handler attribute in the imported content would be stored and rendered as executable HTML (stored XSS) on the Discourse origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:45 — import_remote calls open-uri `open(url)` which follows redirects, so an attacker posts http://embeddable-host/redirect?to=http://169.254.169.254/ and the forum fetches internal URLs despite the host check in TopicRetriever#invalid_host?.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only validates the host of the initial `@embed_url` string (`URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`). But `TopicEmbed.import_remote` then does `open(url).read` (open-uri), which by default follows HTTP redirects. That means a URL on the allowed `embeddable_host` that redirects (e.g., via an open redirect endpoint) to an internal address (like `http://169.254.169.254/...`) would be fetched by the forum, bypassing the intended host restriction. There is no post-redirect host/IP re-validation in `import_remote`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — Throttle key is `retrieved:<embed_url>`, so an attacker hitting embed/best with unlimited unique URLs on the embeddable host (…?a=1,2,3) bypasses the 60s limit entirely and drives unbounded outbound fetches and topic creation.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb, retrieved_recently? uses a Redis key of "retrieved:#{@embed_url}" (the full URL string). That means throttling is per-exact-URL, not per-host or per-client. An attacker can call /embed/best with many unique embed_url values on the allowed host (e.g., same path with different querystrings) and each will bypass the 60s throttle because it produces a new Redis key. Since perform_retrieve then calls fetch_http -> TopicEmbed.import_remote -> open(url).read and TopicEmbed.import (creating a new topic/embed if none exists for that URL), this can drive unbounded outbound HTTP fetches and topic creation (or at least unbounded job enqueues via EmbedController/Jobs::RetrieveTopic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:44 — Each cache-miss retrieve runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously, so N concurrent unknown embed URLs cause N full feed downloads plus N import passes over every feed item — a self-inflicted stampede on the feed host and DB.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` unconditionally does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` whenever `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to HTTP fetch. `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` can synchronously call `poll_feed`, which `open`s `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`, parses the entire feed, and iterates `rss.items.each` calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for every item. The only throttle in TopicRetriever is `retrieved_recently?`, but it is keyed by the specific `@embed_url` ("retrieved:#{@embed_url}"); it does not prevent multiple concurrent retrieves for different unknown embed URLs from each triggering a full feed download + full import pass. So N concurrent cache-miss embed URLs can indeed cause N feed downloads and N full import loops, creating a stampede on the feed host and extra DB work.

matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies that `request.referer` is interpolated into a JavaScript string literal without escaping and explains how a malicious Referer (e.g., containing a quote) can inject script, which is the same XSS vulnerability described in the golden comment. Additional notes about postMessage/origin are extra but don’t change the core issue.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:16 — TOCTOU between `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).first` and `create!` under the unique index: a retrieve job and PollFeed racing on the same URL raise RecordNotUnique, rolling back the topic and failing the job.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-create on a column with a unique index. It first reads `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank enters a transaction and later calls `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` (with a unique index added in `create_topic_embeds` migration). If another worker/process creates the same `topic_embeds.embed_url` after the initial `where(...).first` but before `create!`, `create!` will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, causing the surrounding `Topic.transaction` to roll back and the job/request to fail (there is no rescue/retry here). This race is plausible because multiple ingestion paths exist in the diff (e.g., `Jobs::PollFeed` and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` / `TopicRetriever` can import the same URL concurrently), and the Redis throttle only applies to `TopicRetriever`, not `PollFeed` or multiple pollers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — @post.save(validate: false)` return value is ignored and TopicEmbed.import then unconditionally does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)`, so a failed update is recorded as synced and never retried.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:41 — Spec asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` although the controller enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic; it only passes via inline job execution and asserts nothing about the enqueue payload or the host guard.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmbedController#best` does **not** instantiate `TopicRetriever`; when no topic is found it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. However `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` to be called during the controller action. That expectation is not satisfied by the controller code (unless the job queue runs inline, which the spec does not set up here), and the spec also fails to assert anything about the actual `Jobs.enqueue` call/payload that the controller performs. So the finding correctly identifies a real, verifiable mismatch/defect in the new spec vs the implemented controller behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:36 — The throttle specs stub `retrieved_recently?` itself, so the redis setnx/expire gate they exist to protect is never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the two “with a valid host” throttle examples explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` (`topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)`), so they never execute the real throttling implementation (the Redis `setnx`/`expire` gate inside `retrieved_recently?`). As a result, these specs don’t actually verify the throttle behavior they are ostensibly about; they only verify branching behavior given a mocked return value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — absolutize_urls only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with `/`, leaving `javascript:` and protocol-relative URLs untouched in raw_html posts.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.import, the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook then returns `raw` directly (bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). The HTML is then rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, only `href`/`src` values starting with `/` are rewritten; anything like `javascript:...` or protocol-relative URLs (`//...`) is left intact. Because the content is treated as raw HTML, those schemes could be preserved into rendered output, creating an XSS/vector risk. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no read timeout and open-uri falls back to Kernel#open, so a slow or `|command` URL hangs or executes in the Sidekiq worker.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job does `require 'open-uri'` and then calls `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. That is Kernel#open as extended by open-uri, and it will treat strings beginning with `|` as a command to execute (and can also open local files), so a maliciously configured `feed_polling_url` could execute commands in the Sidekiq process. The “no read timeout” part is less clear because Net::HTTP/open-uri have defaults, but the unsafe Kernel#open behavior with `|command` is a real issue present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:16 — Origin check uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` substring matching rather than equality, accepting any origin that is a prefix/substring of the configured URL.
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:6 — New public embed/best endpoint and its embed.js snippet are unversioned, so any future route/markup change breaks already-deployed third-party host pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new route (`get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'`) and a client snippet (`embed.js`) that hard-codes that path and query param format. However, the proposed finding is about future compatibility (“any future route/markup change breaks already-deployed third-party host pages”), which is speculative and not a concrete defect introduced by this diff. There is no versioning mechanism shown, but lack of versioning is an architectural preference/maintenance concern rather than a verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness problem present in the code as changed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:4 — embed.js assumes host page defines discourseUrl/discourseEmbedUrl and a #discourse-comments element, and throws (appendChild on null) with no guard or documented contract

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the script immediately reads `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)` with no null-check. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, this will throw at runtime (`Cannot read properties of null`). Likewise, `discourseUrl` / `discourseEmbedUrl` are referenced directly (not via `window.discourseUrl`), so if they are not defined by the host page the script will throw a `ReferenceError` when building `iframe.src`. There is no guard or fallback behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — discourse-resize message is only posted once on window.onload, so the host iframe height never updates when the loading page reloads or content changes

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the resize message is sent in window.onload of the embedded iframe. That handler will run every time the iframe document loads. The loading page (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) triggers a full document.location.reload() after 30s, which causes the iframe to reload and thus re-fire window.onload, sending a new discourse-resize message. So the statement that the iframe height “never updates when the loading page reloads” is not verifiable from the diff. The diff also doesn’t introduce any in-iframe dynamic content changes after load that would require continuous resize events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage contract uses the full request.referer as targetOrigin and an undocumented/unversioned {type,height} payload shape
lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 — The --category/-c option was removed without deprecation, so existing disqus import invocations now fail with an unknown-option error

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and also removes the code that read `options[:category]` to determine `category_id`. With Thor, invoking the task with a now-undefined option (e.g. `--category` / `-c`) will raise an unknown-option error. This is a verifiable backward-incompatible behavior change introduced by the diff (no deprecation/compat handling is shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Topic creation switched to TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently dropping the imported created_at and requiring live network fetches of every thread link

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the initial topic/post creation was changed from `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), ...)` to `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does an `open(url).read` (network fetch) and ultimately creates the post without passing any `created_at`, so the original thread timestamp is no longer preserved and the import now depends on live HTTP requests for each thread link.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14 — Controller enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic but the accompanying spec asserts TopicRetriever.new is called directly; caller contract mismatch

adjudication.rationale: Real mismatch: `EmbedController#best` enqueues a background job (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`) when no embed is found, and does not instantiate `TopicRetriever` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` to be called during the controller action. Given the diff, that spec will fail because `TopicRetriever` is only invoked inside `Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute`, not in the controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131 — Post#cook now returns unfiltered raw for raw_html posts, bypassing the after_post_cook plugin filter that existing callers rely on

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now early-returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which skips the existing `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` call entirely. This is directly verifiable in the diff: the plugin hook is only invoked on the default path after `post_analyzer.cook(*args)`. As a result, any plugins relying on the `:after_post_cook` filter to post-process/sanitize/transform cooked content will not run for `raw_html` posts, which is a behavior change/regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:10 — params.require(:embed_url) raises ParameterMissing on a public third-party-facing endpoint instead of returning a defined error response

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best the line `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` intentionally enforces presence of the parameter. In Rails, `ActionController::ParameterMissing` is handled by the framework and results in a 400 Bad Request (not an unhandled 500) unless the app has overridden this behavior. The accompanying spec explicitly exercises the missing-parameter case (`get :best` with no params) and only asserts the response is not successful, indicating this behavior is expected/acceptable. The diff does not show any requirement for a custom error payload or that the exception would be unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:16 — Loading response is served with discourse_expires_in 1.minute, so third-party/CDN caches may pin the placeholder page after the topic exists

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after the `if topic_id` branch. That means the `loading` placeholder page (rendered when `topic_id` is nil and a background job is enqueued) will also be sent with cache headers allowing caching for up to 1 minute. If an intermediary cache/CDN caches `/embed/best?embed_url=...`, subsequent reloads (the loading template triggers `document.location.reload()` after 30s) can keep serving the cached placeholder even after the topic has been created, delaying the appearance of the real embed until the cache expires.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Editing an already-released migration to add `force: true` silently DROPs an existing populated top_topics table on any re-run (db:migrate:redo, staging rebuilds).

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` is destructive: it DROPs the table and all embed mappings if the migration is ever re-run, and makes `change` effectively irreversible/unsafe.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In ActiveRecord, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before creating it. While the table is new in this diff (so a normal first-time migrate won’t drop anything), the code as written is objectively destructive if the migration is ever re-run against a DB where `topic_embeds` already exists (e.g., a partially-applied environment, manual table creation, or other nonstandard state), causing loss of existing embed mappings. The part claiming it makes `change` irreversible is overstated (Rails can still reverse `create_table`), but the data-loss risk from `force: true` is real and directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — embed_url` is a plain `t.string` (varchar(255)) yet stores arbitrary article URLs; longer URLs raise/truncate on insert and the unique btree index has no length guard.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb the column is defined as `t.string :embed_url, null: false` with no `limit`, so it defaults to 255 chars in Rails. The code stores full article URLs in `TopicEmbed.embed_url` (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)` and `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url)`), so URLs longer than 255 will either be rejected (e.g., Postgres VARCHAR(255) length violation) or truncated (some MySQL configs), breaking inserts/uniqueness semantics. This is a concrete schema/correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — add_column :posts, :cook_method, default: 1, null: false` rewrites the entire posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock with no batched backfill, causing extended downtime on large forums.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11 (which aligns with the era of this codebase), adding a column with a non-null default forces a table rewrite and requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration of the rewrite. The migration does not use a safer pattern (add nullable column with no default, backfill in batches, then add default/NOT NULL), so on large `posts` tables this can cause extended lock time/downtime. This is directly implied by the migration as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 — No indexes on topic_id/post_id despite `TopicEmbed.where(topic_id:)` lookups and belongs_to joins; also no FK/dependent cleanup so rows dangle when topics/posts are deleted.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:31 — embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` runs outside a transaction with the post revision, so a failed revise! can leave sha1 and post content out of sync (no backfill/repair path).
app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — <%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby and will raise a SyntaxError whenever the view renders
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using `end if` to close an ERB/Ruby `if` block is invalid syntax and will raise an error at render time; the fix is to use just `end`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage targetOrigin is the full `request.referer` URL, not an origin, so the resize message is never delivered
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that postMessage's targetOrigin is incorrectly set to the full request.referer URL instead of just the origin (scheme+host+port), which causes the resize message to be dropped/not delivered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4 — already-shipped migration edited to add `force: true`, silently dropping an existing top_topics table on replay

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration file `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to change `create_table :top_topics do |t|` into `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it. While this won’t affect a database that has already run the migration under normal `db:migrate`, it is a real correctness risk on any replay path (e.g., `db:migrate:reset`, rollback/re-run, or running the migration against a DB where the table exists), because it can silently drop existing `top_topics` data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44 — spec expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` but the controller enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, so the test cannot pass

adjudication.rationale:
The finding is correct. In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`; it never instantiates `TopicRetriever`.

However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the test at/around line 44 in the diff) expects `TopicRetriever.new` to be called and then `retriever.retrieve` to run. Since the controller path under test only enqueues `:retrieve_topic`, those expectations cannot be satisfied, so the spec will fail as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:44 — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` invokes a scheduled job synchronously as a library call, leaking the job layer into request-triggered code

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` is indeed a synchronous invocation of a job class, but in this diff it is not “request-triggered code”: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, and *that* background job calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`. So the call happens in a Sidekiq job context, not directly in the request/response path. This is more of an architectural/style concern (job class reuse) than a clear defect introduced by the diff, and it’s not verifiably a bug/security/correctness problem from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:47 — inline `require 'ruby-readability'` inside `import_remote` instead of a top-level require

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` includes `require 'ruby-readability'` because the gem is declared in the Gemfile with `require: false`, so it will not be auto-required. Requiring inside the method is a valid lazy-loading pattern in Ruby; `require` is idempotent and cached after the first load, so this does not introduce a correctness, security, or clear performance defect in the diff. At most it's a stylistic preference about where to place the require.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — inline `require 'simple-rss'` inside `poll_feed` rather than at file top with the other requires

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `require 'simple-rss'` placed inside `poll_feed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) while other requires are at the top. However, this is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect: Ruby allows `require` inside methods, and in this case it can be intentional to lazy-load the gem only when feed polling is actually executed. At most it’s a style/performance preference, not a clear problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:1 — require_dependency 'nokogiri'` misuses the autoload-reload require for a gem; should be plain `require

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`. While `require_dependency` is typically used for files under Rails autoload paths to support class reloading, using it on a gem (like `nokogiri`) still effectively loads it (it ultimately delegates to `require` and tracks dependencies). The diff does not show any concrete malfunction, security issue, or correctness defect caused by this line—at worst it's an unconventional choice / style or minor dev-mode behavior difference, not a clearly verifiable problem introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — require_dependency 'email/sender'` is unused dead code in this job

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the top-level `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is never referenced anywhere in the file. The job only looks up a user and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`, and there are no constants/methods from `Email::Sender` used. This makes the require appear to be unnecessary/dead code introduced by the diff (at minimum an avoidable load/side-effect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:37 — embed.permalink` locale key is never referenced by any view or model

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink` under `config/locales/server.en.yml`, but the new/modified code in this diff only references `embed.title`, `embed.start_discussion`, `embed.continue`, `embed.loading`, and `embed.imported_from` (e.g., in `app/views/embed/*.erb` and `TopicEmbed.import`). No reference to `embed.permalink` is visible in the diff. However, an unused locale key is not a functional bug/security/correctness defect by itself; it’s at most dead/extra translation data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5 — no guard for a missing `#discourse-comments` element or undefined `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl` globals; script throws on the host page

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the IIFE immediately reads `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` into `comments` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)`. If the host page does not include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and this will throw. The script also directly references `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` when building `iframe.src`; if either global is not defined on the host page, it will raise a `ReferenceError` before any other logic runs. No guards are present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:16 — origin check uses `indexOf` substring matching against the configured URL, a fragile and spoofable comparison
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue flag the same core problem: using `indexOf`/substring matching to validate the origin is insecure because it can be spoofed by a malicious domain containing the trusted URL as a substring (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss:1 — new standalone embed.js/embed.css.scss bundles are not added to any asset precompile list, so they will 404 in production
app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — absolutize_urls` duplicates the same rewrite loop for `a[href]` and `img[src]

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, there are indeed two very similar loops: one over `fragment.css('a')` rewriting `href`, and one over `fragment.css('img')` rewriting `src`. However, this is just code duplication/DRY refactoring opportunity, not a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff. Both loops are functionally appropriate because they operate on different tags/attributes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:49 — user lookup by `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is duplicated verbatim in Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show duplicated code: both `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` and `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` perform the same lookup `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and return if blank. However, this is just a DRY/refactoring concern, not a verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change. The duplication does not cause incorrect behavior on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:4 — the `start_discussion` branch is unreachable in practice since a rendered topic view always has posts

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the `best.html.erb` template is rendered only when `topic_id` is found and `@topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` is created. The template checks `@topic_view.posts.present?` to decide between showing `embed.title` vs `embed.start_discussion`. Given this is a "best" view (`{best: 5}`), it is plausible (and consistent with the intent) that `@topic_view.posts` can be empty for topics with no qualifying "best" posts (e.g., a topic with no replies), making the `start_discussion` branch reachable. The diff does not prove that `TopicView` always returns at least one post for this mode, so calling it unreachable is a misreading/speculation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 — --category` option and its lookup removed without replacement, silently dropping category support from the importer

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the associated lookup (`Category.where(name: options[:category])...`) and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The importer now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and neither this call nor `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` accepts or forwards a category. This is a functional regression/backward-incompatible change: Disqus imports can no longer target a specific category, and there’s no replacement mechanism in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read` in import_remote has no open/read timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge remote page can hang a Sidekiq worker indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, the code does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`, which uses `open-uri` to fetch and then fully read the remote response into memory with no explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` or maximum size. This can block a Sidekiq worker for a long time on slow/unresponsive endpoints and can also consume excessive memory on very large responses. The lack of any explicit timeout/size controls is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` has no timeout, so a hung feed server stalls the scheduled job (and, via TopicRetriever, a request-triggered job) with no recovery.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does call `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without passing explicit timeout options, and it does not rescue network errors. However, the finding claims there is “no timeout” and that it can hang indefinitely. With Ruby’s `open-uri`, there are built-in default `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` values (implementation-dependent), so the diff alone does not verifiably show an unbounded hang due to “no timeout”. The lack of explicit timeouts may be a robustness concern, but the specific claim is not strictly provable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — Redis throttle uses non-atomic SETNX+EXPIRE; a crash between the two leaves `retrieved:<url>` with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval of that embed URL.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code throttles by calling `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two distinct Redis commands; if the process crashes or loses connection after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the key can be left without a TTL. That would cause `retrieved_recently?` to return true forever for that embed URL, permanently throttling retrieval. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads every 30s unconditionally with no attempt cap, so any permanently failing retrieval creates an infinite reload loop hammering the server.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the embedded script always runs `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` with no condition or retry cap. If the background retrieval never creates the embed/topic (e.g., invalid URL, host mismatch, network failure), the page will remain on `loading` and keep reloading indefinitely, repeatedly hitting the `embed#best` endpoint every 30 seconds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:21 — The 60s throttle is consumed even when retrieval fails/raises and is never cleared, so the 30s client reload always re-renders `loading` and retrieval is retried at most every 60s forever.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the throttle key is set with `setnx` and explicitly given a 60s TTL via `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. So it is cleared automatically after 60 seconds, even if `perform_retrieve` fails/raises, meaning it is not “never cleared” nor “forever”. Also, the client won’t “always” re-render `loading`; once `TopicEmbed` exists, `EmbedController#best` renders the topic view. While it’s true the throttle is consumed even if retrieval errors (because the key is set before `perform_retrieve`), that behavior is not inherently a defect and the rest of the finding is factually incorrect per the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — No per-item rescue: one item with nil `content`/`title` or a failing import aborts the whole feed poll, silently skipping all remaining items.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop `rss.items.each do |i|` performs `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no `begin/rescue` inside the loop. If any item has `i.content == nil` (so `.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`), or if `TopicEmbed.import`/underlying DB calls raise for a single item, the exception will abort `poll_feed` immediately and the remaining RSS items won’t be processed. Since `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set, a single bad item can effectively stop the whole poll run until the next scheduled execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs a full synchronous feed fetch+import inline inside the RetrieveTopic job on every embed miss, so unauthenticated page views can trigger repeated full feed polls.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously before doing the normal HTTP fetch. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs a real network fetch (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates all items importing them. This path is reachable from an embed page view: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` when no embed exists, even for `current_user` nil (unauthenticated). Although `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles by `embed_url` for 60 seconds, an embed miss still triggers a full feed poll whenever `perform_retrieve` runs (and can be repeated across many distinct embed URLs), so the finding about inline synchronous feed fetching/import being triggered by unauthenticated embed traffic is verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:10 — RetrieveTopic has no error handling around network retrieval; open-uri failures propagate and Sidekiq default-retries the fetch up to 25 times per embed URL.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:12 — sidekiq_options retry: false` combined with no rescue means a single transient feed error drops the poll entirely with no logging or alert.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does set `sidekiq_options retry: false` for `Jobs::PollFeed` and the job does not rescue around `open(...)` / `SimpleRSS.parse`, so a transient exception would cause that particular run to fail without Sidekiq retrying it. However, the proposed finding overstates the impact in ways not verifiable from the diff: scheduled jobs will typically run again on the next hourly recurrence, and Sidekiq will normally log unhandled exceptions even when `retry: false` (the diff does not show logging being suppressed). Thus the “drops the poll entirely with no logging or alert” portion is not supported by the change, and the remainder is more a design choice than a clear defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5 — No null check on `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')`; if the container is missing or the script runs before it, `comments.appendChild` throws and the embed never loads.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the code does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe)`. If the element with id `discourse-comments` is not present in the DOM (or the script executes before it exists), `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a runtime error, preventing the embed from loading. There is no guard or deferred execution beyond the IIFE.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — postMessage` targetOrigin is the full `request.referer` URL (or blank when absent), which fails origin matching so the parent never receives the resize and the iframe stays collapsed.

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb the code calls parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>'). The second argument (targetOrigin) must be either "*" or an origin string of the form scheme://host[:port], not a full URL with a path/query. Since request.referer will typically be a full page URL (e.g., http://eviltrout.com/2013/...), browsers will reject it (often throwing a DOMException) or it won’t match the parent window’s origin, so the resize message won’t be delivered and the iframe height won’t update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — creator.create` failure is silently swallowed inside the transaction (no error surfaced/logged), so failed imports look like successes and are retried forever.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the creation path wraps `post = creator.create` in a transaction and only proceeds if `post.present?`. If `PostCreator#create` returns `nil`/blank on failure (which this code anticipates by checking `present?`), the failure is not raised, logged, or otherwise surfaced—execution just exits the transaction without creating a `TopicEmbed` record. Callers like `Jobs::PollFeed` ignore the return value, and `EmbedController#best` will continue to enqueue retrieval jobs/render loading whenever no `TopicEmbed` exists, so a persistent create failure can lead to repeated retries with no visibility into the underlying error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place, so a retried/repeated import appends the footer again and changes the SHA1, causing spurious revisions.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the passed-in `contents` String in place. Because Ruby strings are mutable and passed by reference, any caller that reuses the same String object across multiple `import` calls (e.g., `contents = ...; TopicEmbed.import(..., contents); TopicEmbed.import(..., contents)`) will get the footer appended repeatedly. That will change `content_sha1` on subsequent calls and can trigger unnecessary revisions and duplicated “Imported from” footers in the stored post content. This side effect is directly verifiable from the diff and is a correctness defect (unexpected mutation of input).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key` is computed but never used: no Last-Modified/ETag conditional fetch, so every hourly poll re-downloads and re-imports the entire feed.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the method `feed_key` (lines ~17-19) computes and memoizes a Redis-style key based on the feed URL, but it is never referenced anywhere in `execute` or `poll_feed` (or elsewhere in the diff). The job always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` each run, i.e., an unconditional re-download of the feed. While `TopicEmbed.import` will prevent duplicate topic creation for already-seen `embed_url`s (and only updates when `content_sha1` changes), the lack of any use of `feed_key` / conditional fetch means the job still fetches and processes the full feed every hour, making the “computed but never used” part a verifiable defect and the “no conditional fetch” implication accurate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` caches the transient `loading` response, so a client may keep seeing a stale loading page after the topic exists.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after the `if topic_id ... else render 'loading'` branch. That means the rendered `loading` response (when `topic_id` is nil and a background job is enqueued) will also be sent with cache headers for 1 minute. Since the loading page itself triggers reloads every 30 seconds, an intermediary cache (browser/proxy/CDN) honoring those headers can serve the cached loading page even after the topic/embed has been created, causing clients to see stale loading until the 1-minute TTL expires.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:32 — Tests stub the private methods (perform_retrieve, retrieved_recently?) they claim to exercise, so only the two-line `retrieve` guard is verified and the redis throttle, PollFeed fallback and import_remote paths are untested.

adjudication.rationale: The TopicRetriever specs do stub internal/private behavior rather than exercising it. In the “valid host” context they explicitly stub `retrieved_recently?` to true/false and only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is called. In the other cases they set expectations that `perform_retrieve` is never invoked. As a result, none of the actual implementations of `retrieved_recently?` (the Redis setnx/expire throttle) or `perform_retrieve` (PollFeed fallback, TopicEmbed existence check, and `import_remote` fetch) are tested by these specs; they primarily validate the single guard line in `retrieve` and the `invalid_host?` predicate. This is a real, verifiable gap in the tests added in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12 — Every test stubs poll_feed, so the actual feed logic (SimpleRSS parse, missing-user return, i.link vs i.id fallback, content.scrub/unescapeHTML, TopicEmbed.import call) is completely untested.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb all examples set expectations on `poller.poll_feed` (`expects(:poll_feed).never/once`), which stubs the method and prevents the real `poll_feed` implementation from running. As a result, none of the logic inside `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` added in the diff (SimpleRSS.parse/open, user lookup/early return, link/id fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls) is exercised by these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 — The "topic retriever" test asserts on a TopicRetriever mock although the controller enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic; it never verifies the job args (user_id/embed_url) nor that the 'loading' template is rendered.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no topic_id is found it does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and `render 'loading'`; it never instantiates `TopicRetriever` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` expects `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` in the “tells the topic retriever to work…” example, so that spec will fail against this implementation. The spec also doesn’t assert that the job was enqueued with `user_id`/`embed_url` or that the `loading` template was rendered, which are the actual behaviors in the controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:10 — The postMessage resize handshake (layout sender + embed.js origin check/height application) has no JS or view test; the loose `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` check would pass an incorrect-origin test unnoticed.
